timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only server event stream with no projected semantic events; used only for manifest accounting and completion evidence.
Session index tying the serial session id to the single main wire file.

Serial main trajectory: explored pandas internals, wrote the entire source tree, packaging, docs, and tests, debugged test failures, fixed groupby and expanding-window code, verified setup and edge cases, then closed.

parallel.requirements: The parent had the full prompt requiring DataFrame and Series apply/map/applymap, groupby support, rolling and expanding windows, progress bars, automatic workers, memory-fs and pipe transports, exception handling, global configuration, cross-platform behavior, setup.py, and __init__.py exports.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split work into package-source implementation for agent-0, packaging/docs/placeholders for agent-1, and a later pytest-writing verifier for agent-2; the parent retained final orchestration but did little direct implementation.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote the pandarallel package and registered DataFrame, Series, GroupBy, RollingGroupby, ExpandingGroupby, and Rolling APIs, but omitted plain Expanding registration. Agent-1 wrote setup and docs. Agent-2 wrote tests only.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All children wrote directly into the shared /workspace tree under scoped file ownership, returned completed summaries, and the parent ran a final tree listing plus local pytest before responding.
parallel.verification: Verification consisted of agent-0 smoke tests across transport modes, agent-2's 41 local pytest cases, and the parent's final pytest rerun; no official submit tool was available inside the trajectory.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation failed 24 of 217 tests. Observable gaps include omitted plain Expanding.parallel_apply and a child-reported rolling step limitation, plus reliance on local tests that did not expose those hidden cases.

serial.requirements: The serial agent used the same prompt and recognized the required package structure, setup metadata, core pandas monkey-patching API, groupby, rolling and expanding windows, memory-fs/pipes, progress, and exception handling.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor owned implementation, packaging, tests, debugging, and final verification, using a todo list for sequencing rather than delegating to children.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote all package modules itself, explicitly imported and patched both Rolling and Expanding, implemented positional groupby reconstruction, and then edited groupby/rolling/expanding modules after local tests exposed failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were created in one workspace by the same actor, with setup, docs, package modules, and tests assembled before final verification and response.
serial.verification: The serial run ran a 41-test local pytest suite, diagnosed a rolling-groupby mismatch and an expanding kwargs TypeError, fixed them, ran setup.py verify, edge-case checks, editable install checks, and a final pytest rerun.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation still failed 4 of 217 tests, but the mounted evidence does not expose the failed testcase names; remaining defects appear ordinary implementation gaps rather than coordination errors.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the broad Pandarallel task, but its delegated implementation contract omitted plain Expanding despite the prompt's rolling and expanding requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized and implemented the broader expanding-window surface by patching pandas Expanding as well as groupby expanding.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important requirement difference is plain Expanding coverage: parallel left it out of the child brief and final registration, while serial included it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into package source, packaging/docs, and tests across three children, with the parent orchestrating and then closing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, packaging, testing, debugging, and closure in the main trajectory with no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent file creation but introduced a child-brief boundary; serial preserved requirement context in one owner throughout implementation and fixes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel briefs set non-overlapping file scopes and a detailed API list, but the package-source brief did not carry the plain Expanding requirement into the child contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent handoff and retained implementation context while adding Expanding support and later editing Expanding kwargs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The missing requirement crossed a parallel parent-to-child boundary; serial did not have that boundary and kept the requirement in the main implementation loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel package code registered DataFrame, Series, groupby, RollingGroupby, ExpandingGroupby, and Rolling support, with concise per-group get_group assembly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial package code registered DataFrame, Series, groupby, Rolling, Expanding, RollingGroupby, and ExpandingGroupby, then repaired positional grouping and Expanding kwargs failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial implemented a wider API and debugged hidden-sensitive pandas 2.3 behavior; parallel's implementation stayed at the narrower child contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The two initial children completed and returned via AgentSwarm, and the later verifier child completed and returned before the parent final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; results and fixes stayed in the main actor's working context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no missing join or trapped child result; the material issue is what the implementation child was asked to build, not result retrieval timing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into the same workspace but with explicit disjoint scopes: agent-0 wrote package source, agent-1 wrote packaging/docs, and agent-2 wrote tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files from the main actor and then edited the same owned package files during debugging.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete collision or overwrite appears in parallel; the shared-state difference is scoped concurrent construction versus serial single-owner edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel accepted after child smoke tests, a 41-test verifier suite, and a parent rerun of that local suite; the tests did not include the omitted plain Expanding API.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used local tests as well, but its main loop saw failures, fixed groupby and expanding-window defects, ran setup.py verify, edge-case checks, and a final pytest rerun.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's verification fed directly back into source edits, while parallel verification stayed within the delegated test suite and did not surface the missing Expanding registration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 1605 agent seconds with 35 LLM requests and three children, then closed after the parent final pytest run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 1622 agent seconds with no subagents, more token use, and a longer single-owner debugging loop before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run timed out, but serial spent more integrated effort on debugging before closure and achieved 20 more official testcase passes.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations make this a both_fail pair: parallel passed 193 of 217 and serial passed 213 of 217. The best-supported score-gap contributor is not a timeout or raw child count but the parallel handoff boundary: the parent delegated source implementation with a detailed API contract that omitted plain pandas Expanding, and the child implementation omitted that registration. Serial kept implementation in one trajectory, patched Expanding, and iterated through failing groupby and expanding tests before final checks.
parallel_contributors: Implementation child brief omitted plain Expanding despite the prompt's expanding-window requirement.
Parent accepted local child-generated tests that covered groupby expanding but did not expose missing plain Expanding registration.
Agent-0 reported a remaining rolling step limitation that was not pursued before closure.
serial_contributors: Single main owner registered Expanding.parallel_apply in core and retained context across implementation and verification.
Serial debugging fixed groupby positional regrouping and Expanding kwargs issues after local test failures.
Serial ran setup.py verify, edge-case checks, editable import checks, and final pytest before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's groupby implementation used direct get_group chunks and manual concat, while serial rebuilt grouped subsets from positional arrays.
Parallel __init__ exported only pandarallel and __version__; serial also exported MEMORY_FS_ROOT and NB_PHYSICAL_CORES.
Packaging and documentation content differed, but the mounted evidence does not tie those differences to the official score gap.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors to a score gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a pass/fail discordance
